entry.title: The Architecture of the Loft
entry.summary: A deep dive into the interconnected Chicago underground of the 1990s and beyond, where the lines between jazz, minimalism, and electronic textures dissolved in the heat of warehouse collaboration.

entry.title: Jazzmatazz & Beyond Vol. 1
entry.summary: A journey through the jazz-hip hop lineage, from Guru's revolutionary 1993 sessions with jazz royalty, through Madlib's Blue Note explorations and Nujabes' Tokyo meditations, to the Brainfeeder generation and London's new wave. The story of a family reunion that never ended.

entry.title: Fuego Latino: A Journey Through Latin Soul, Jazz & Rhythm
entry.summary: From the Afro-Cuban jazz pioneers of 1940s Harlem to the Buena Vista Social Club's Havana revival, this show traces the pulse of Latin music through three explosive decades. entry.title: Quiet Village: The Exotica Dream
entry.summary: Three sonic architects craft imaginary islands from Hollywood studios—Les Baxter's orchestral jungles, Martin Denny's bullfrog serenades, Arthur Lyman's vibraphone twilights. Post-war suburban escapism crystallized in stereo.

entry.title: Bristol Dusk Downtempo
entry.summary: Hazy trip-hop from Bristol's golden era—Massive Attack's dub echoes, Portishead's noir soul, and the downtempo waves that defined the 90s.

entry.title: Desert Sessions Vol. 2: Generator Parties
entry.summary: A journey through the sun-baked, fuzz-drenched world of desert rock — from the illegal generator parties of Palm Desert to the modern psychedelic revival. This episode explores the origins of the genre, the breakthrough of Songs for the Deaf, and Josh Homme's resurrection after his near-death experi

entry.title: Electric Strings: A Tribute to Michal Urbaniak
entry.summary: An extended memorial tribute to the Polish electric violin pioneer Michal Urbaniak (1943-2025), exploring his legacy alongside Jean-Luc Ponty, Jerry Goodman, and the fusion violinists who transformed the instrument.

entry.title: Slavic Passions
entry.summary: A journey through the emotional intensity of Eastern European masters - from the rivers of Bohemia to wartime Moscow

entry.title: Sacred Echoes: 800 Years of Spiritual Music
entry.summary: A journey from medieval monks to Bach—800 years of sacred music spanning mystics, rebels, and mathematical geniuses.

entry.title: African Legends: East African Fusion Flows
entry.summary: 1970s Ethio-jazz, Ugandan psych-rock, and Ethiopian azmari swing—featuring Mulatu Astatqé, Akira Ishikawa, and Mahmoud Ahmed.

entry.title: The Dreamer's Catalog
entry.summary: A journey through artists who made visionary music that the world wasn't ready for - from Shuggie Otis's psychedelic soul to Lonnie Liston Smith's cosmic jazz to Marcos Resende's lost Brazilian masterpiece.

entry.title: Grandmaster Improvisations
entry.summary: Investigating the profound link between the logic of Chess and the structure of Jazz. Exploring music as a strategic game of pattern recognition, featuring the stories of Anthony Braxton, Sun Ra, and Charlie Parker.

entry.title: Brigitte Psychédélique
entry.summary: A cosmic tribute to Brigitte Bardot (1934-2025), celebrating her psychedelic pop legacy and the swinging sounds of 1960s French yé-yé.

entry.title: The Zorchman's Psychobilly Special
entry.summary: A late-night journey through psychobilly's unholy origins - from the 1950s primal scream of The Phantom to the Klub Foot chaos of The Meteors. Featuring P. Paul Fenech's cult-leader charisma, the kinetic energy of the wrecking pit, and the strange Lynchian surrealism that defined a genre.

entry.title: The Melancholy Disciples
entry.summary: A journey through three generations of melancholy indie rock - from Johnny Marr's guitar revolution to The Cure's emotional mastery to The Twilight Sad's Scottish walls of sound

entry.title: Captain Beefheart Legacy: From Trout Mask to Swordfish
entry.summary: Tracing Don Van Vliet's avant-garde blueprint from Safe As Milk through Trout Mask Replica, and its direct influence on Tom Waits' Swordfishtrombones

entry.title: Circuit Dreams: The Architecture of Sound
entry.summary: A journey through experimental electronica, from Prefuse 73 to Boards of Canada and Flying Lotus.

entry.title: Nocturnal Dreams: A Chopin Journey
entry.summary: An intimate exploration of Frédéric Chopin's nocturnes, those moonlit masterpieces that transformed the piano into a vessel for pure emotion. Performed by Adam Harasiewicz, winner of the 1955 International Chopin Piano Competition.

entry.title: Jazz Rock Revolution of the 70s
entry.summary: A journey through the explosive 1970s fusion movement where jazz improvisation collided with rock energy, funk rhythms, and electronic experimentation. From Miles Davis' electric breakthrough to the virtuoso fireworks of Mahavishnu Orchestra and Return to Forever.

entry.title: Spatial Minimalism
entry.summary: Italian electronic pioneer Roberto Cacciapaglia alongside Terry Riley, Suzanne Ciani, and other minimalist masters exploring the boundaries of ambient soundscapes

entry.title: Japanese Fusion: East Meets West in Sound
entry.summary: A sonic journey through Japan's groundbreaking fusion movement of the 1970s and early 80s, where traditional Japanese sensibilities merged with American jazz, funk, and electronic experimentation. Featuring Hiroshi Suzuki, Ryo Kawasaki, Jun Fukamachi, Haruomi Hosono, and other pioneers who created a

entry.title: Kosmische Musik: A Journey Through Krautrock
entry.summary: An exploration of Germany's revolutionary 1970s rock scene, featuring motorik rhythms, cosmic explorations, and avant-garde experimentation from the pioneers who changed music forever.

entry.title: Duende - The Soul of Flamenco
entry.summary: A passionate journey through flamenco music featuring legendary artists Paco de Lucia, Camaron de la Isla, Ketama, and Carlos Heredia. From traditional forms to nuevo flamenco, experience the duende - that inexplicable magic that transforms sound into pure emotion.

entry.title: Black President: The Revolutionary Sound of Fela Kuti
entry.summary: A celebration of Fela Anikulapo Kuti, the Nigerian musician who invented Afrobeat and used his music as a weapon against corruption and military dictatorship. This show explores his incredible journey from London jazz student to Africa's most challenging and charismatic performer.

entry.title: Latin Jazz Corner
entry.summary: The fiery rhythms of Latin jazz, blending Afro-Cuban percussion with bebop sophistication.

entry.title: Modal Masters
entry.summary: A celebration of the golden age of jazz innovation, from bebop pioneers to spiritual jazz explorers.

entry.title: The Genius of Bach
entry.summary: A journey through Bach's most profound keyboard works, featuring legendary performances by Glenn Gould and Rosalyn Tureck.

entry.title: Indie in 2000 (Cartesia Edition)
entry.summary: Exploring the indie rock explosion at the turn of the millennium with essential tracks from the year 2000.
